Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Great Falls MT
1211 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

 - Snow continue through the morning hours today across Southwest
   Montana.

 - Next opportunity for mountain precipitation arrives Monday
   morning and persist through the day.

 - Strong and gusty winds return to the plains by Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Moderate (0.5" to 1.0" per hour) to at times heavy (1.0" to 1.5" per 
hour) snowfall will persist through the remainder of the overnight 
hours across Southwest Montana, with generally light snowfall 
extending as far north as the Island Ranges of Central Montana as a 
shortwave embedded within northwest flow aloft moves over the 
Northern Rockies. Snowfall rates will decrease rapidly near sunrise 
this morning, with generally light snow lingering over the Madison 
and Gallatin ranges through the early afternoon hours before 
ending. As snowfall rates decrease through sunrise this morning 
temperatures will fall into the 20s, which combined with wet 
surfaces will support the opportunity for a flash freeze any many 
roadways across Southwest Montana. This flash freeze will make 
travel hazardous through the remainder of the morning, with 
gradually improving conditions through the noon hour as skies clear 
and temperatures warm to near freezing.

Otherwise a relatively benign pattern is expected through the 
remainder of the weekend as upper level ridging builds in over the 
Northern Rockies through this timeframe. This upper level ridge will 
ridge will help to keep temperatures near to slightly above normal 
through Sunday, with overall dry conditions and light winds winds 
expected. The exception to these light winds will be in the north-
south orientated valleys of Southwest Montana where southerly winds 
will be breezy and gusty, most notably in the Madison River Valley 
where there is a 30% chance that wind gusts exceed 40 mph on Sunday.

The upcoming work week looks to be active as the upper level flow 
becomes more zonal in nature, with several shortwaves rippling 
through and over the Northern Rockies. While high winds are not 
expected at this time across Southwest through North Central 
Montana, southwest to west surface winds will be strong and gusty at 
times along the Rocky Mountain Front and across the Montana Hwy 
200/US Hwy 87 corridors; particularly from Tuesday through Friday. 
Temperatures will moderate over the plains thanks to these gusty 
winds, with the valleys of Southwest and Central Montana remaining 
near to slightly below normal thanks to strong inversions setting up 
over the valley floors. Several opportunities for mainly mountain 
precipitation will arrive through the work week thanks to the 
shortwaves rippling through the zonal flow, with the best 
opportunity arriving Monday morning and lasting through Monday 
night. - Moldan

&&

.AVIATION...
28/06Z TAF Period.

For the northern-most terminals (KLWT, KGTF, KCTB and KHVR), VFR 
conditions will prevail throughout this TAF period. KCTB will see 
a brief increase in winds around 08Z, before mellowing back down 
to a steady northwest wind around 10 kts by 12Z. All four 
terminals will see an uptick in this northwest wind around 16-18Z,
before becoming light and variable by the evening. 

For the southern-most terminals (KBZN, KEKS, KWYS and KHLN), 
conditions remain much less simple. KBZN and KEKS will see a 
transition from rain to snow in the first few hours of this TAF 
period, becoming all snow by around 07-08Z. KHLN will go straight 
into snow around 07Z. The snow will cause reduced visibilities and
lower ceilings, with LIFR to even VLIFR conditions continuing to 
be well within the realm of possibility. The exception is KHLN, 
which is more likely to only see conditions drop down to IFR at 
the worst. The bulk of the snow should cease this morning around 
12-13Z. However, some lingering flurries are possible throughout 
the rest of the morning. -Dzomba

&&

.TFX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Winter Weather Advisory until 11 AM MST this morning for 
Beaverhead and Western Madison below 6000ft-Big Belt, Bridger 
and Castle Mountains-Elkhorn and Boulder Mountains-Gallatin 
Valley-Madison River Valley-Missouri Headwaters-Northwest 
Beaverhead County-Ruby Mountains and Southern Beaverhead

and Madison County Mountains and Centennial Mountains.

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 27 at 11:02PM MST until November 28 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Great Falls MT
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations between 2 and 7
inches below 7000 feet, with 5 to 9 inches of additional snow
expected above 7000 feet. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Gallatin and Madison County Mountains and Centennial
Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Flash freezing conditions expected Saturday
morning. Plan on hazardous conditions even after precipitation
ends.
